approach: Three parts. (1) Config: [history] gains optional cutover_job; athena.toml sets it to 20261025-001232-vesh. (2) Cutover action in athena-core. records_import.rs gets a cutover variant of the importer that appends to a records branch that already holds the landing record, publishes via append_to_remote, and self-checks with a verifier that ignores non-records/ paths. gh.rs adds a cutover routine: C0 is the host_commit of the landing record whose commits name the job. It imports (only if import-manifest.json is absent at the records tip), then writes legacy-exempt.json (only if absent) from legacy_exempt_record/legacy_exempt_change. Both steps are idempotent, keyed on file presence at the remote records tip. The routine is called (a) after the landing record is written in free land_pr, through a new default-no-op LandingRecords hook, so existing fakes and LandPr literals are untouched, and (b) as a catch-up at the end of Athena::try_reconcile, which land and status already run first. (3) Gate: attribution.rs gets cutover_commit(git, job) reading the landing at the records tip; history.rs check_history becomes a router. With no cutover_job, no records branch, no landing for the job, or C0 not an ancestor of the tip, it runs today's check_history_with_exempt(None) unchanged. Otherwise it runs legacy::check_attribution_with_legacy (old rules up to C0 with the exempt list from the record; records-only walk after C0), converts findings to violations (new Rule::Attribution), and runs gitleaks over the tip. check_history_with_exempt stays non-routing so the legacy check at C0 cannot recurse. manage.rs is untouched because it calls check_history. ci.yml's history job keeps its name and adds a 'git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records' step before the check.

decisions.choice: Route inside history::check_history (not in Athena::check_history in manage.rs).
decisions.reason: manage.rs is not a listed file and the CLI and CI both go through check_history. Routing there means no CLI change, and every call with no cutover_job takes the identical old path.

rejected.option: Edit manage.rs/main.rs to call a new function
rejected.why: Touches unlisted files and widens the change.
The legacy check calls it at C0, whose athena.toml has cutover_job, so it would recurse.

decisions.choice: Cutover-only importer entry point that appends onto the existing records tip, leaving import_records strict.
decisions.reason: The landing record is written before the import, so the branch already has a tip and import_records would return AlreadyImported. The old importer tests and their strict self-check keep passing; the new path adds a non-strict verifier that ignores paths outside records/ and the manifest.

rejected.why: C0 is the host commit of the landing record, which does not exist until the landing is written, so C0 is unknown.

decisions.choice: Idempotence by file presence at the freshly synced remote records tip: import-manifest.json for the import, legacy-exempt.json for the exempt record, each checked and written separately.
decisions.reason: Matches the reading's assumption. It also repairs a crash between the two writes, and a second reconcile writes nothing.

rejected.option: A local marker file or state flag
rejected.why: Not shared across machines and can disagree with the branch.

decisions.choice: Hook through a default-no-op method on the LandingRecords trait, with cutover_job held in GitLandingRecords (builder method), not a new LandPr field.
decisions.reason: LandPr is built by struct literal in many tests; a new field would break them. Fakes of LandingRecords need no change.

rejected.option: Run the cutover in Athena::land_pr after land_pr returns
rejected.why: Would need the landing record's host commit re-derived; the hook has the facts in hand, and reconcile catches any miss anyway.

decisions.choice: A cutover failure is a warning in land and a reported skipped line in reconcile, never a failure.
decisions.reason: The merge and landing record are done and stay done (same stance as the landing-record warning); the catch-up retries on the next land or status.

rejected.why: The merge has already happened and cannot be undone.

decisions.choice: Cutover is active only when the landing record names the job and C0 is an ancestor of the tip. A missing legacy-exempt record after that is a visible finding (LegacyExemptMissing, already in legacy.rs), not a silent pass.
decisions.reason: Meets 'before the records branch shows C0, exactly as today' while never silently weakening the check once C0 shows.

rejected.option: Fall back to old rules when legacy-exempt.json is missing
rejected.why: It would hide a half-finished cutover.

decisions.choice: Trailers keep being written; no change to trailer writing.
decisions.reason: Request defers ending them to a later job.

files.purpose: Add cutover_job = "20261025-001232-vesh" to [history], with a comment saying what it does. The exempt list is unchanged.

risks.risk: CI's history job would fail in the window where the landing record shows C0 but legacy-exempt.json is not yet written (LegacyExemptMissing).
risks.mitigation: The import and the exempt record are written back to back in the landing hook, and the reconcile catch-up repairs a crash on the next land or status. The finding is deliberate, not a silent pass.

risks.risk: The importer's refusal and self-check semantics change if the strict path is edited by mistake.
risks.mitigation: Leave import_records and verify_import untouched and add separate cutover functions; the existing importer tests run unedited.

risks.risk: After the cutover, commits after C0 skip the old content checks (personal data, size, secrets by config), so coverage narrows.
risks.mitigation: This is what the request says (after C0 only by records). Gitleaks still runs over the whole tip, and the decisions entry names the narrowing.

risks.risk: Adding Rule::Attribution breaks exhaustive matches elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Grep for matches on Rule; clippy and the build catch the rest.

risks.risk: reconcile.rs and lib.rs are outside the brief's file list.
risks.mitigation: Both edits are minimal and required (the reconcile step the request names; the violation type). Flagged as an open question so the reviewer can accept or redirect.

risks.risk: A history test needs a records branch with valid intent, landing and legacy-exempt records, which is fiddly to build.
risks.mitigation: Reuse the helpers and record builders in legacy.rs tests and the attribution tests.

risks.risk: Pushes to the remote records branch race with other writers.
risks.mitigation: append_to_remote already retries against a moving tip with an expected-tip guard; the idempotence checks re-read the synced tip each time.

demonstrations.method: A scratch-repository test in gh.rs. It builds a repo with a bare remote and a fake PrHost whose job id equals the configured cutover_job, then drives the land path (free land_pr with GitLandingRecords::for_remote(..).with_cutover(job)) through a merge. It then reads the remote records branch: the landing record's host_commit equals the resolved C0; an import commit exists with import-manifest.json whose C0 is that commit and for which verify_cutover_import passes; legacy-exempt.json parses with 7 entries (six plus 02837e0), each with a non-empty reason.
demonstrations.observes: The test asserts the landing file, import-manifest.json, the imported records/ files and the 7-entry legacy-exempt record on the remote athena/records, and C0 == the landing's host_commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the landed hook, the records branch holds only the intent and landing: no manifest and no legacy-exempt.json, so the assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: A catch-up test in reconcile.rs or gh.rs. Set up a remote whose records branch holds the intent and a landing for the cutover job but no import. Run Athena::reconcile (the same step land and status call at their start) and assert the import commit (with manifest) and legacy-exempt.json now exist, with the commit count increased by exactly two. Run reconcile again and assert the remote records tip is unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Records tip moves on the first reconcile, with a manifest and 7 exempt entries present (a real write, not an empty no-op); the second reconcile leaves the tip identical.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the catch-up in try_reconcile, the first reconcile leaves the tip unchanged and the manifest assertion fails; without the presence checks, the second run adds a commit or errors.

demonstrations.method: A history.rs test on a scratch repo. Main has a pre-C0 commit that breaks the old rules (for example a governed-content change with no landing) and is excused only if legacy-exempt.json names it. It also has a post-C0 commit with no trailer and no prediction, matched by an intent and landing on athena/records. The test sets cutover_job in athena.toml at C0 and calls check_history. Variants: the pre-C0 commit unexempted yields a violation naming it (old rules); the post-C0 commit with its landing yields none; the post-C0 commit with no landing yields an Attribution violation.
demonstrations.observes: Violations list is empty for the records-only post-C0 commit and non-empty exactly for the pre-C0 old-rule breach and for the unattributed post-C0 commit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the router, the post-C0 trailerless commit is judged by the old trailer and invariant rules and fails; without the attribution hand-off, an unattributed post-C0 commit passes.

demonstrations.method: No new code path runs when cutover_job is None, or Some but with no records branch or no landing for it. Add small tests that set cutover_job with no records branch, and with a records branch holding no landing for the job, and assert the report equals check_history_with_exempt(None). Run the existing suite unedited.
demonstrations.observes: Every pre-existing history, legacy, attribution and lifecycle test passes with unmodified expectations; the new fallback tests show identical reports.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the router engaged without a resolved C0, the existing history tests that have no records branch would produce attribution findings (a missing branch is a finding) and fail.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the files, plus a config test parsing athena.toml. The new test in config.rs parses the repo's athena.toml (and a toml with and without cutover_job) and asserts cutover_job == Some("20261025-001232-vesh") (and None when absent). Review ci.yml: job id history keeps name 'the full history', with a 'git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records' step before 'athena check --history'.
demonstrations.observes: The parsed value is Some(this job's id) from athena.toml, None when absent; the diff shows the fetch step precedes the check step and the name line is unchanged.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, deny_unknown_fields rejects athena.toml with cutover_job set, so the parse test and every config-reading test fail.

demonstrations.method: Review the diff: docs/decisions.md has a new decision entry covering C0, import at C0, the legacy-exempt record, catch-up reconcile, behavior before C0, and trailers still written; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
demonstrations.observes: Both files show added entries naming each topic, written for an outside reader.

demonstrations.method: Run the lint, format and test gates over the whole workspace.
demonstrations.observes: No warnings. Then cargo fmt --all --check reports no diff and cargo test --locked passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Unformatted code, an unused import or a non-exhaustive match on the new Rule::Attribution would fail clippy, fmt or the build.

open_questions: reconcile.rs and gate lib.rs are not in the brief's file list but the design needs them (the reconcile step named in the request; a Rule for attribution violations). Accept, or should the findings reuse an existing Rule and the catch-up live in gh.rs, with reconcile.rs calling only a one-line entry point?
Whether the 'job's own id' (20261025-001232-vesh) is the id the landing record will name in its commits' job field. The plan assumes so, as the request says.
Which athena.toml exempt list the legacy-exempt record is built from: the list at C0 (planned) or the current tip's. They are identical today (seven entries).
I did not read the existing legacy.rs and attribution test helpers in detail, so I could not confirm how much of them the new history test can reuse.
